First, we plot the graph of $y=3^{x}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14220062/assets/1cd695e6f1fab35a692fde9003d452862db33a894c23657eb87f8d773de8cbb9.png)

Next, we plot the graph of $y=5(3^x).$ To do this, we scale the graph above by a factor of $5.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,5),$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14220062/assets/1c92ea5f3cbfd40bd0dc384b152f6166c27400dbedd93a9c8333195950e7f9c3.png)

Finally, we plot the graph of $y=5(3^x)-3.$ To do this, we shift the above graph $3$ units down. The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,5)$ to $(0,2),$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=-3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14220062/assets/d8e8cdccd58a9f1f21c8c2bf0a4a8c08e9c263c4fe91cc92e2bee334de057116.png)
